original_question: Construct examples of Finsler metrics of constant curvature on S^2 that are not Zoll and such that they admit no Killing vector field.
target_in_paper: Section 8.5, Problem 8.5.2: "Construct examples of Finsler metrics of constant curvature on S^2 that are not Zoll and such that they admit no Killing vector field."
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem in the paper almost verbatim: it has the right ambient manifold (S^2), the right geometric category (Finsler metrics), the right curvature condition (constant curvature in the Finsler/flag-curvature sense used in §8.5), and the two essential exclusions (not Zoll; no Killing vector field).
missing_details: The paper’s curvature notion here is Finsler flag curvature, not Riemannian sectional curvature; in the surrounding discussion of §8.5 this is the setting of constant positive flag curvature, normalized nearby in Problem 8.5.1 to flag curvature 1.
To make the question stand-alone, 'Zoll' should be defined as in the immediately preceding paragraph: all geodesics are closed and have the same common length.
'Admit no Killing vector field' should be stated as 'admit no nontrivial Killing vector field' to remove the implicit convention that the zero field is always present.

No reversibility assumption should be added; nearby the paper notes that the reversible constant-flag-curvature-1 case on S^2 is just the round Riemannian metric, so the intended problem is genuinely in the nonreversible realm.

The nearby dichotomy implies a hidden reformulation: any sought example must lie in the 'all geodesics are closed' case and be non-Zoll, because the alternative case necessarily carries a Killing vector field.
refined_question: Can one construct explicit Finsler metrics F on S^2 of constant positive flag curvature (equivalently, after normalization, flag curvature 1) that are not Zoll—in the sense that not all geodesics are closed with the same common length—and that admit no nontrivial Killing vector field?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the dichotomy stated immediately before Problem 8.5.2, can one construct a Finsler metric on S^2 of constant positive flag curvature that lies in the 'all geodesics are closed' case, is not Zoll, and admits no nontrivial Killing vector field?
justification: The draft is already the paper’s exact target: Section 8.5, Problem 8.5.2. The only refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are to spell out that the curvature under discussion is Finsler flag curvature in the positive-curvature S^2 setting of §8.5, to unpack the paper’s definition of 'Zoll' from the preceding paragraph, and to make explicit that 'no Killing vector field' means no nontrivial Killing field. The alternate formulation is justified by the explicit nearby dichotomy: every constant-flag-curvature metric on S^2 falls into one of two cases, and the first case necessarily has a Killing vector field, so any example with no Killing field must belong to the second ('all geodesics closed') case and be non-Zoll. No algebraic ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers are relevant to this geometric problem.
